The Discourse on the Charge of Impurity:
Is it the case that an Arahant emits semen?
Yes, it is.
Is there in an Arahant lust, sensual lust, obsession by sensual lust, the fetter of sensual lust, the flood of sensuality, the yoke of sensuality, and the hindrance of sensual desire?
One should not say so... [etc. ...
Is there no lust in an Arahant, no sensual lust, no obsession by sensual lust, no fetter of sensual lust, no flood of sensuality, no yoke of sensuality, and no hindrance of sensual desire?
“Yes.

“If it is true that for an Arahant there is no lust, no sensual lust, no obsession by sensual lust, no fetter of sensual lust, no flood of sensual desire, no yoke of sensual desire, and no hindrance of sensual desire, then surely you should not say:
‘An Arahant has impure semen emissions.’”

Is there impure emission of semen in an ordinary person; and is there in him lust, sensual lust, obsession by sensual lust, the fetter of sensual lust, the flood of sensual desire, the yoke of sensual desire, and the hindrance of sensual desire?
Yes. Is there impure emission of semen in an Arahant; and is there in him lust, sensual lust, obsession by sensual lust … [and so on] … the hindrance of sensual desire? No.
It should not be said so...
[as before] ...Does the Arahant have impure emission of semen? Yes. Is there in him lust, sensual lust, obsession by sensual lust... [as before] ...the hindrance of sensual desire? Yes.
Is there impure emission of semen in an ordinary person (puthujjana), yet no lust, no sensual lust, no obsession by sensual lust, nor the hindrance of sensual desire in him?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is there impure emission of semen in an Arahant?
“Yes,” he said. “In what sense?
“Because, indeed, deities belonging to Māra’s host were offering impure semen to the Arahant.”
Do the deities belonging to the host of Māra provide an arahant with impure emissions of semen?
Yes. Is there impure semen emitted by the deities belonging to the host of Māra? Yes.
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is it not the case that there is no impurity or emission of semen among the deities belonging to Māra’s host?
Yes, it is.
If there is no impure emission of semen among the deities belonging to Māra’s host, then indeed it should not be said:
“The deities belonging to Māra’s host bring about an impure emission of semen for an Arahant.
Do the deities belonging to Māra’s host bring about an impure emission of semen for an Arahant?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Do the deities belonging to Māra’s host bring their own impure emissions of semen, do they bring the impure emissions of semen of others, and do they bring his impure emissions of semen?
You should not say so… [and so on]… No, indeed.
Do the deities of Māra’s host neither provide for themselves, nor for others, nor for him an impure emission of semen?
Yes.
If the deities of Māra’s host neither provide for themselves, nor for others, nor for him an impure emission of semen, then indeed it should not be said: [that they do so].
“Deities belonging to the host of Māra provide an arahant with impure semen.
Do deities belonging to the host of Māra provide an arahant with impure semen?
Yes.
"Do you say that deities belonging to Mara’s host discharge semen into the pores of an Arahant?
You certainly should not say so...
[and so on] ... Do you say that deities belonging to Mara’s host discharge semen into an Arahant?"
“Yes.
“For what reason?
“Indeed, it is because I wish to cause doubt to arise.”

“Yes,” [you say]. “Then does an Arahant have doubt regarding the Teacher, doubt regarding the Dhamma, doubt regarding the Saṅgha, doubt regarding the training,

doubt regarding the past, doubt regarding the future, doubt regarding both the past and the future, or doubt regarding phenomena that have arisen through specific conditionality and dependent origination?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … An arahant has no doubt regarding the Teacher, no doubt regarding the Dhamma, no doubt regarding the Saṅgha, no doubt regarding the training,
no doubt regarding the past, no doubt regarding the future, no doubt regarding both the past and the future, and no doubt regarding specific conditionality and dependently arisen phenomena?
“Yes.

“If it is true that there is no doubt in an Arahant regarding the Teacher … [and so on] … nor doubt regarding phenomena that have arisen dependently through specific conditions, then indeed you should not say:
‘An Arahant has doubt.’”
An ordinary person has doubt; he has doubt regarding the Teacher ... [and so on] ... doubt regarding phenomena that have arisen dependently through specific conditions, is that so?
Yes. An Arahant has doubt; he has doubt regarding the Teacher ... [and so on] ... doubt regarding phenomena that have arisen dependently through specific conditions, is that so?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Does an Arahant have doubt?
Yes. Does he have doubt regarding the Teacher? No. … [as before] … Does he have doubt regarding the phenomena that have arisen dependently through specific conditions? Yes.
“Does an ordinary person have doubt? Does he not have doubt regarding the Teacher? … [and so on] … does he not have doubt regarding phenomena that are dependently arisen through specific conditions?
One should not say this … [and so on] … “Does an Arahant have impure semen emissions?”
“Yes,” he replied.
“If that is so, from what is the emission of semen by an arahant the result?
“It is the result of what has been eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted.”
Is the emission of semen by an Arahant the natural result of what he has eaten, drunk, chewed, or tasted?
Yes. Then is there an emission of semen for everyone who eats, drinks, chews, or tastes? Yes. [If so,] then all those who eat, drink, chew, or taste must have an emission of semen.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it the case that for whoever eats,
drinks, chews, or tastes— provided they are living— all of them possess impurity, namely, emitted semen?
Yes, it is.
"Boys eat, drink, chew, and taste; do boys have impurity and the emission of semen?
"One should not say so.
"Eunuchs eat, drink, chew, and taste; do eunuchs have impurity and the emission of semen?"
It should not be said so … [as before] … Devas eat, drink, chew, and taste; do devas have impurity, such as the discharge of semen?
It should not be said so … [as before] …
Is the emission of impure semen by an Arahant the natural outflow (*nissanda*) of what has been eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted?
Yes. Does he have a physical receptacle (*āsaya*) for it? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it the case that the excrement and urine of an Arahant— the outflow of what has been eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted— is his "residue" (āsaya)?
Yes, it is.
Is the discharge of impure semen by an Arahant the result of what has been eaten, drunk, chewed, or tasted, and does he have a physical receptacle for it?
One should not say so... [as before] ...
Is the discharge of impure semen by an Arahant the result of what has been eaten, drunk, chewed, or tasted, and does he not have a physical receptacle for it?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is the excrement and urine of an Arahant the residue of what has been eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted, and does he have no receptacle for it?
You must not say so… [and so on].
Is it the case that an arahant has impure emissions of semen? Yes.
Then an arahant would practice sexual intercourse, would produce sexual desire, and would dwell in a bed crowded with children.
Would he enjoy Kāsī sandalwood, wear garlands, scents, and unguents, and accept gold and silver?
Certainly not.
Yet there is impure semen emitted by an ordinary person (*puthujjana*), and an ordinary person might engage in sexual intercourse.
Would he engage in sexual intercourse, dwell in a bed crowded with children, enjoy Kāsī sandalwood,
wear garlands, scents, and unguents, and accept gold and silver?
Yes, he would.
Is it possible that an arahant could have an emission of impure semen; that an arahant could engage in sexual intercourse; that an arahant could produce the desire for sexual intercourse;
that an arahant could dwell in a bed crowded with children; that an arahant could enjoy Kāsī sandalwood; that an arahant could wear garlands, scents, and unguents;
or that an arahant could accept gold and silver?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … There is impure semen discharged by an Arahant, yet an Arahant would not engage in sexual intercourse, would not produce sexual desire,
would not dwell in a bed crowded with children, would not enjoy Kāsī sandalwood, nor would he use garlands, perfumes, or ointments.
"Would he accept gold and silver?
"Yes.
"An ordinary person may have an emission of impure semen, yet an ordinary person does not engage in sexual intercourse."
"Would he engage in sexual intercourse, dwell in a bed crowded with children, enjoy Kāsī sandalwood, wear garlands, scents, and ointments, and accept gold and silver? "Certainly not;
one should not say so."
Is it the case that an Arahant has impure emission of semen? Yes.
But has not lust been abandoned by the Arahant, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, rendered non-existent, and subject to non-arising in the future?
“Yes.

“If it is true that for an Arahant lust has been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, rendered non-existent, and is subject to non-arising in the future, then surely it should not be said:
‘There exists in an Arahant impure semen discharged.’”

Is it the case that an Arahant emits impure semen? Yes, you say. But has not the Arahant abandoned hatred? … [and so on] … Yes. Then how can he emit impure semen? [He cannot. Therefore, your proposition is false.
Delusion has been abandoned… conceit has been abandoned… wrong view has been abandoned…
Doubt has been abandoned;
sloth has been abandoned;
restlessness has been abandoned.
Is shame abandoned …pe… is lack of moral dread abandoned,
cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, rendered non-existent, and subject to non-arising in the future? Yes.

If, for an Arahant, lack of moral dread has been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like the stump of a palm tree, rendered non-existent, and subject to non-arising in the future, then surely it should not be said:
"An Arahant has impure semen emissions. Is it the case that an Arahant has impure semen emissions?
“Yes.
“But has the path not been developed by the Arahant for the abandoning of lust?
“Yes.”
If the path has been cultivated by an Arahant for the abandoning of lust, then surely it should not be said:
"There is impure semen discharged by an Arahant.
Is there impure semen discharged by an Arahant?
“Yes,” he said.
“Is it not the case that for an Arahant the foundations of mindfulness have been developed for the abandoning of lust?
… [and so on] … the right efforts have been developed?”
The bases of psychic power have been developed;
the faculties have been developed;
the powers have been developed... [and so on]...
"Are the factors of enlightenment developed? "Yes.
"If the factors of enlightenment are developed for the abandoning of lust in an Arahant, then indeed you should not say—"
“There is impure semen discharged by an Arahant.
Is there impure semen discharged by an Arahant? Yes.
Is it not the case that for an Arahant,
the path has been cultivated for the abandoning of hatred … [and so on] … for the abandoning of delusion … [and so on] … for the abandoning of moral fearlessness? … [and so on] …
"Are the factors of enlightenment developed for the abandoning of non-fearlessness in an Arahant? "Yes.
"If the factors of enlightenment are indeed developed for the abandoning of non-fearlessness in an Arahant, then, alas, you should certainly not say—"
“There is impure semen discharged by an Arahant.
Is there impure semen discharged by an Arahant? Yes.

Now, surely the Arahant—one who is free from lust, free from hatred, and free from delusion; one who has done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained his own goal, utterly destroyed the fetters of existence, completely liberated through final knowledge;

one for whom the crossbar is lifted, the moat is filled in, the pillar is uprooted, who is without bars, noble, with banner lowered, with burden dropped, detached, a victor in the well-fought victory—for him suffering is fully understood, its origin is abandoned, [its cessation is realized, and the path leading to its cessation has been developed].
"Has cessation been realized, has the path been developed, has that which is to be directly known been directly known, has that which is to be fully understood been fully understood,
has that which is to be abandoned been abandoned, has that which is to be developed been developed, and has that which is to be realized been realized? "Yes, it has."
If an Arahant is one who is free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion,
who has done what was to be done … [as above] … and has realized what was to be realized, then indeed, sir,
you should not say: "There is impure semen emitted by an Arahant."
Is there impure emission of semen for an arahant?
For an arahant skilled in his own doctrine (sadhamma), there is impure emission of semen; for an arahant skilled in another's doctrine (paradhamma), there is no impure emission of semen.
Is there impure emission of semen for an arahant skilled in his own doctrine?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then does an Arahant who is skilled in others’ qualities have impure emissions of semen?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Is it the case that for an Arahant skilled in the supreme Dhamma there is no impure emission of semen?
Yes. Is it the case that for an Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma there is no impure emission of semen? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is passion abandoned by an Arahant who is skilled in his own doctrine, yet does he still have impure semen emitted?
Yes.
Is lust abandoned by an Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma, yet does he still have impure semen emissions?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is hatred abandoned by an Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma... [and so on] ...?
Delusion has been abandoned … [and so on] … lack of moral dread has been abandoned; yet he still emits impure semen, is it not?
Yes, he does.
Is fearlessness of wrongdoing abandoned by an Arahant skilled in the supreme Dhamma? [If you say] "it is," does that Arahant still have impure emissions of semen?
You should not speak thus...
[and so on] ...The path has been cultivated by an Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma for the abandoning of lust... [and so on].
The factors of enlightenment,
when developed … [lead] to the abandoning of hatred … [lead] to the abandoning of delusion … [and so on].
If the path has been developed for the abandoning of fearlessness of wrongdoing … and the factors of enlightenment have been developed, does he still experience the emission of impure semen?
Yes, he does.

For an Arahant skilled in the supreme Dhamma, the factors of enlightenment have been developed for the abandoning of fearlessness; does it follow that such a person still has impurity or the emission of semen?
One should not say so … [as before] … An Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma is one who is free from lust, free from hatred, and free from delusion … [as before].
That which is to be realized has been realized; yet does he still have impure emissions of semen?
Yes. Is an Arahant—one skilled in the qualities of others, free from lust, free from hatred, and free from delusion … [and so on] …? Yes.
That which is to be realized has been realized; does he still have impure semen emissions?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
For an Arahant skilled in the supreme Dhamma, lust has been abandoned; does he still have impure semen emissions? One should not say so.
“Yes,” you say.
“Is passion abandoned by an Arahant who is skilled in the True Dhamma, and does he not have any impure emission of semen?
You must not say so… [and so on].
Has hatred been abandoned by the Arahant who is supremely skilled;
…pe… has delusion been abandoned;
…pe… has moral shamelessness been abandoned? Is it not the case that there is no impure emission of semen for him?
“Yes.
“Then, for an Arahant who is skilled in his own Dhamma, has fearlessness (anottappa) been abandoned? Is it not the case that there is no impurity or emission of semen in him?
“One should not say so” … [and so on] … “One should not say so.”
For the Arahant, who is supremely skilled, the path has been developed for the abandoning of lust …pe… the factors of enlightenment have been developed …pe… for the abandoning of hatred …pe…
If the path has been developed for the abandoning of delusion …pe… for the abandoning of moral shamelessness,
and the factors of enlightenment have been developed, is it not the case that there is no impurity or emission of semen for him?
“Yes,” [you say].

“For an Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma, the factors of enlightenment have been developed for the abandoning of fearlessness-of-evil; yet it must not be said that such a one has impure emissions of semen?
… [as before] … No, you should not speak thus.
Is it not the case that for an Arahant who is skilled in the supreme Dhamma, free from lust, free from hatred,
and free from delusion … [as before] … having realized what was to be realized, there is no impurity or emission of semen?
Yes, it is.

"Is it not the case that for an Arahant, skilled in the True Dhamma, free from lust, free from hatred, and free from delusion—[as described at length]—who has realized what is to be realized, there is no impurity or emission of semen?
"One should not say so... [and so on].
Is it the case that an arahant has impure emissions of semen?
Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“Bhikkhus, when those ordinary bhikkhus who are accomplished in virtue fall asleep mindful and clearly comprehending, no impurity is emitted.
And even for those outside ascetics who are free from lust for sensual pleasures, no impurity is emitted.
It is impossible, bhikkhus, it cannot happen, that an arahant should emit impurity.”
Is it indeed a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, it should not be said—
“There is impure semen discharged by an Arahant.
Should it not be said:
“There is the taking of life by another for an Arahant”?
“Yes.
“But surely others would provide for an Arahant the requisites of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal provisions for use in sickness?
“Yes.”
If others were to provide an arahant with robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick, then indeed it should be said:
"There is the providing of requisites by others to an arahant.

Is it the case that there is the providing of requisites by others to an arahant, on the grounds that others might provide an arahant with robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Can others bestow upon an Arahant the fruit of stream-entry, or the fruit of once-returning, or the fruit of non-returning, or Arahantship?
“One should not say so,” [the respondent replies]. …pe… [as before].
The Discussion on the Taking of What Is Not Given is finished.
